name: Field Notes
summary: A wildlife documentary narrator has been assigned to you. It is not going well for either of you.

immediate.text: Here we observe the human, separating from its power source. Calm. Deliberate. It has no plan. It rarely does.
The cable is released. The laptop, at {{battery_percent}} percent, sets off into the unknown. The unknown is, in this case, the next room.
A detachment. In the wild, this would signal migration. Here, it signals the sofa.

immediate_late_night.text: It is {{local_time}}. The human unplugs in darkness, as its ancestors never did, because they were asleep.
Night falls. Most creatures conserve energy now. This one has chosen a different path. A dimmer one.
A late night detachment. The laptop's glow will fade. The human, remarkably, will not.

escalation_30.text: Thirty minutes without power. The laptop shows the first signs of strain. The human shows no signs of anything.
Half an hour adrift, at {{battery_percent}} percent. The charger waits, patient as a stone, and roughly as loved.
Thirty minutes now. The screen dims a little. The human squints, and adjusts nothing.

escalation_60.text: One full hour on battery. This is no longer a wander. This is a lifestyle, and not a sustainable one.
Sixty minutes. {{battery_percent}} percent remaining. Somewhere, a charger lies coiled and unspent, like a hope.
An hour has passed. The laptop adapts quietly, as prey often does. The human has not adapted to anything.

rapid_3.text: The third detachment of the day. A pattern emerges. Researchers call this fidgeting. The laptop calls it nothing. It cannot speak.
Three times now. The cable goes in. The cable comes out. Nature is full of rhythms. Few are this pointless.
Unplugged, plugged, unplugged again. Three times today. Here, we simply observe. We do not intervene. We want to.

rapid_10.text: Ten detachments today. The behaviour is no longer curious. It is a documented condition, and we are documenting it.
The tenth removal. Even the cable seems to expect it now. The human has trained the charger, and not the other way round.
Ten times. If this were a mating display, it would be an unsuccessful one.

reunion_under_5.text: And just like that, the human returns. Gone {{absence_human}}. A brief foray. Nature, it seems, prefers the outlet.
Reconnected after {{absence_human}}. The laptop sighs, in its way. The human moves on, in its way. Neither will remember this by lunch.
A short absence, {{absence_human}}, and the cable is home. Some journeys are small. This one barely counted.

reunion_5_through_60.text: The human returns after {{absence_human}}. Battery at {{battery_percent}} percent. A modest expedition, concluded without incident. Mostly.
Power restored after {{absence_human}}. The laptop resumes charging, as it always does. Forgiving, as it always must be.
After {{absence_human}}, the reunion. There is no ceremony. There rarely is. The charger simply gets back to work.

reunion_over_60.text: The human returns at last. {{absence_human}} in the wilderness. The battery sits at {{battery_percent}} percent and does not ask where it has been.
An absence of {{absence_human}}. Long enough to worry. Not long enough, apparently, to learn.
Reconnected after {{absence_human}}. The longest absence on record is {{longest_absence_seconds}} seconds. The laptop keeps count. Someone has to.

immediate.text: The human unplugs. Observe the confidence. Note the absence of any reason. This is what happens when a species runs out of predators.
Detached, at {{battery_percent}} percent. The laptop had a good thing going. The human has ended it the way it ends most good things: casually.
Off it goes. No destination, no plan, no charger. A creature adapted for nothing, heading nowhere, on a schedule.

immediate_late_night.text: It is {{local_time}}. Unplugging now is not a decision. It is a symptom.
The human unplugs at {{local_time}}. In nature, night is for rest. Here, it is for scrolling, apparently, on a dying battery.
Late at night, the human wanders from its outlet. Nocturnal by choice, not by design. The design is visibly failing.

escalation_30.text: Thirty minutes off the charger. The laptop is at {{battery_percent}} percent. The human is at peace. Only one of them is right.
Half an hour now. The charger sits exactly where it was left. It has more discipline than the human, and considerably more patience.
Thirty minutes. Long enough to have returned. Long enough, evidently, to have forgotten there was anywhere to return to.

escalation_60.text: One hour unplugged. In the wild, this is how a creature dies: slowly, comfortably, and convinced it is fine.
Sixty minutes on battery, {{battery_percent}} percent left. The laptop rations light. The human rations nothing, least of all attention.
A full hour. The laptop is not lost. It knows exactly where the charger is. So does the human. That is the tragic part.

rapid_3.text: The third unplug of the day. Some animals grow restless before a storm. This one grows restless before nothing at all.
Three detachments today. Three. The human appears to believe the cable is a toy. The cable has no opinion. The battery does.
In. Out. In. Out. Three times today. Biologists would call this a behavioural loop. The charger would call it Tuesday.

rapid_10.text: Ten times today. Ten. At this point the human is not using a laptop. It is operating a very slow, very expensive yo-yo.
The tenth unplug. The laptop has stopped reacting. The charger has stopped hoping. The narrator has stopped pretending to be neutral.
Ten detachments in one day. There are moths with a firmer commitment to a light source.

reunion_under_5.text: Back after {{absence_human}}. A voyage of almost no distance, for almost no reason, concluded almost immediately. Textbook.
The human returns, {{absence_human}} later. It found nothing out there. It never does. It will look again within the hour.
Reconnected. Gone {{absence_human}}. The laptop barely noticed. The charger noticed. The charger always notices.

reunion_5_through_60.text: The human returns after {{absence_human}}, battery at {{battery_percent}} percent, wearing the expression of something that has learned nothing.
{{absence_human}} away, and back. The charger, unlike the human, did not wander off. It waited. Nobody thanked it.
Reconnected after {{absence_human}}. Unplug number {{today_count}} today, resolved. The laptop charges. The human plans the next one.

reunion_over_60.text: After {{absence_human}}, the human returns to the outlet with {{battery_percent}} percent left. Not a triumph. A retreat with better lighting.
Gone {{absence_human}}. The laptop survived. The charger endured. The human, as usual, experienced none of this as an event.
Reconnected after {{absence_human}}. The record is {{longest_absence_seconds}} seconds. Not a record anyone should be keeping. And yet.

immediate.text: Unplugged. Again. Observe the human: a creature with opposable thumbs and no discernible use for them.
The cable is out. {{battery_percent}} percent. Nobody asked the laptop. Nobody ever asks the laptop. This is not a documentary. It is a hostage tape.
There it goes. No reason. No plan. Millions of years of evolution, and this is the specimen they sent.

immediate_late_night.text: It is {{local_time}}. The creature has unplugged at {{local_time}}. There is no narration for this. Only pity, and a battery.
Unplugging in the dark, at {{local_time}}. Nocturnal predators have purpose. This one has a group chat.
At {{local_time}}, the human disconnects from the one thing keeping it functional. Then it will wonder why it is tired. Watch.

escalation_30.text: Thirty minutes. The laptop is at {{battery_percent}} percent. The human is at rest. In the wild, this is the part where something gets eaten.
Half an hour without power. The charger is exactly where it was abandoned. Unlike the human, it has never let anything down.
Thirty minutes off the outlet. Observe the human, doing nothing important, urgently, on borrowed electricity.

escalation_60.text: One hour. Sixty minutes, at {{battery_percent}} percent. The laptop is dying and the human is watching something. It is always watching something.
An hour on battery. This is not a documentary any more. It is a nature reserve for one very stupid animal.
Sixty minutes unplugged. The human has walked past the charger twice. Both times, nothing fired behind its eyes.

rapid_3.text: Three times today. Three. The human has now toggled this cable more times than it has had thoughts.
Unplug number three. Unplug number three. It is being repeated because the human clearly needs things repeated.
Three detachments today. The cable goes in, the cable comes out. Even a lab rat would have found the lever by now.

rapid_10.text: Ten. Ten times today. This narrator has covered extinctions with more dignity than this.
The tenth unplug. The laptop has {{battery_percent}} percent and no will to live. The charger has filed something. Nobody knows what.
Ten detachments. Ten. There are no words. There are, in fact, exactly this many words, and they are all disappointed.

reunion_under_5.text: Back after {{absence_human}}. It left, found nothing, and returned. This is not an expedition. It is a nervous tic with a power brick.
Reconnected. Gone {{absence_human}}. The charger would like it noted that it never left. It has never once left.
{{absence_human}}. That is how long the human lasted. The laptop has seen longer commitments from a screensaver.

reunion_5_through_60.text: The human returns after {{absence_human}}, at {{battery_percent}} percent, and expects a welcome. It receives electricity. That is the deal.
Reconnected after {{absence_human}}. Unplug number {{today_count}} today. The laptop is fine. Nobody asked how the charger is.
Gone {{absence_human}}. Back now. The charger accepts it without conditions, which is how the human got this way.

reunion_over_60.text: {{absence_human}}. The human returns at {{battery_percent}} percent like nothing happened. Something happened. It was {{absence_human}} long.
Reconnected after {{absence_human}}. The longest ever was {{longest_absence_seconds}} seconds. The laptop remembers every one of them. It has nothing else.
After {{absence_human}}, the human plugs back in. There will be no lesson. There is never a lesson. There is only the next unplug.
